data.title: Lightfastness Testing of Colored Pencils
data.author: picture
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了艺术作品中色彩持久性的重要性，即“耐光性”，以及如何选择耐光材料以防止褪色。作者Sarah Renae Clark在过去六个月中对50多个彩铅品牌进行了耐光性测试，将色卡暴露在阳光下并记录变化。文中解释了什么是耐光性、其重要性、测量方法（如蓝羊毛尺度、ASTM D6901标准等），以及作者的测试结果和见解。耐光性对想要作品长久保存的艺术家尤其重要，无论是展示、赠送还是出售。然而，对于仅注重创作过程或数字使用的作品，耐光性则不那么关键。文章旨在帮助艺术家选择合适的材料，以确保作品的持久鲜艳。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同介质（如笔、颜料、纹身墨水）的耐光性和持久性

不同观点：
• smokel 分享了使用符合 ISO 12757-2 标准的档案墨水进行绘图的经验，发现这些绘图在一年内褪色。他指出，该标准适用于存档（如保存在盒子里），而非长期展示。同时提到 BIC 圆珠笔的蓝色墨水在阳光下会变黑。
• hoistbypetard 表示尽管对色素的耐光性没有直接兴趣，但觉得 smokel 的测试和研究非常有趣，并认为这些通常被视为个人审美偏好而非可量化指标。
• humblebeekeeper 从纹身墨水的角度参与讨论，指出紫外线会使纹身颗粒变小，并分享了与淋巴系统相关的有趣事实。
• mattgrice 详细讨论了不同颜色的耐光性，指出粉色和橙色通常不耐光，红色颜料如镉虽耐光但有毒。还提到了一些传统但易褪色的颜料如玫瑰红和茜素 crimson。
• burnt-resistor 对整个测试过程表示赞赏，称之为“艺术版的 Project Farm”。
• chris_st 提到一本关于水彩测试的书，并分享了自己在黑色笔耐光性测试中的经验，发现 Micron 笔具有耐光性。
• sllabres 分享了其对喷墨打印机墨水和保护膜的测试结果，发现红色墨水在 4 个月内褪色，而黑色墨水 20 年后仍保持较好。
• wrp 对机械铅笔芯进行了类似测试，推荐使用 Staedtler Mars Micro Color 以获得耐光性。
• dylan604 对粉色在测试图表中表现最差的现象表示好奇，想知道其实际视觉效果是否完全消失或仅是数据上接近于零。
• CGMthrowaway 提出天然颜料通常不如合成颜料耐光，并询问如果偏好天然颜料的色彩质量，是否选择测试中表现较差的铅笔是合理的。
• bayindirh 简短指出 Caran d'Ache 以其高品质和价格著称。
• __mharrison__ 表示曾认为 Prismacolors 是彩色铅笔的终极选择，对测试结果表示遗憾。
• hoppyhoppy2 提供了一个存档链接，指向一个关于光耐久性的网站。
• gennarro 对测试图片的质量和测试条件（如每天 6 小时阳光照射）表示质疑，并询问固定剂是否有助于测试。

补充讨论：
- 测试条件和方法的多样性，如不同的墨水、颜料、铅笔和保护膜。
- 天然与合成颜料的耐光性对比。
- 不同颜色（尤其是红色和粉色）在耐光性上的差异。
- 用户对品牌和价格的看法，如 Prismacolors 和 Caran d'Ache。
- 实际测试结果和标准（如 ISO 12757-2）之间的差距。
- 纹身墨水在紫外线下的变化作为一个有趣的跨领域讨论点。

44468753.article_content:
Lightfast Testing: 50+ Coloured Pencil Brands
By
Sarah Renae Clark
|
2025-04-22T16:47:32+10:00
April 5th, 2025
|
Have you ever spent hours on a piece of artwork, only to watch it fade over time? It’s a frustrating reality for many artists, and it all comes down to something called ‘lightfastness’ – a medium’s resistance to fading over time when exposed to light. If you want your work to last, choosing supplies with good lightfast ratings is essential.
But how do we know which art supplies will hold up over time? Some brands advertise their materials as “lightfast,” but do their claims hold up in real-world conditions? That’s exactly what I set out to test. Over the past 6 months, I’ve exposed swatches of coloured pencils and markers to sunlight and tracked their changes. I also compared my results to industry-standard lightfastness tests to see how different brands truly perform.
In this blog, I’ll break down:
What is Lightfastness?
Why Does it Matter?
How is Lightfastness Measured? And how I measured it.
My 6-month Lightfast Testing Results and Insights
Whether you’re a professional artist selling your work or a hobbyist who wants their art to last, this guide will help you make informed choices about your supplies.
>>> CLICK HERE TO JUMP TO THE RESULTS!
What is Lightfastness?
Lightfastness refers to how well a colour resists fading when exposed to light over time.
Art supplies that are “highly lightfast” can often last 100 years or more in museum conditions. While other art supplies might fade as soon as they see the sun. This is especially important for artists who want their work to last for years without significant colour shifts.
Fading occurs because some pigments break down when exposed to light, particularly ultraviolet (UV) rays from the sun. Different art supplies use different types of pigments and binding materials, which means some colours are naturally more resistant to fading than others. While some art materials are designed to be highly lightfast, others may start losing their vibrancy after just a few days of exposure to light.
Understanding lightfastness helps artists make better choices about their materials, whether they’re working on personal projects, commissions, or selling their art. In the next sections, we’ll explore why this matters and how it’s tested.
Why is Lightfastness Important?
Nobody wants to pour time and creativity into an artwork only to see it fade away. That’s why lightfastness (how well your colours resists fading over time) is worth paying attention to. Whether you’re colouring for fun, creating gifts, or selling your work, fading colours can be a letdown.
Art you want to display
If you enjoy displaying your artwork, lightfastness is something to consider. You probably want your art to stay true to its original colours. Artwork displayed in well-lit areas – especially near windows – can fade quickly if created with non-lightfast materials. Choosing the right supplies helps preserve your work so it can be enjoyed for years without noticeable fading or colour shifts.
Art you want to give away
If you love sharing your artwork with friends and family, lightfastness is something to consider. A beautifully coloured piece might look stunning at first, but if it starts to fade after a few months, it could lose its charm. Choosing lightfast materials ensures that your gifts remain as vibrant and meaningful as the day you gave them.
Art you want to sell
If you’re selling artwork, ensuring that your materials are lightfast is essential. Buyers expect their purchases to last, and if a piece fades within months or years, it can damage your reputation as an artist. Many professional artists specifically choose lightfast materials to guarantee their work remains vibrant for generations.
When is Lightfastness NOT Important?
Lightfastness isn’t always a top priority, and that’s completely okay! If your focus is on the process rather than the final piece, then fading might not matter to you at all. This includes things like:
Personal work where you’re experimenting, practising, or simply enjoying the creative flow.
Projects that you plan to scan or photograph the final piece and use it digitally or for prints rather than keeping the original.
Artwork that stays safely tucked away in a sketchbook or colouring book, away from sunlight.
In these cases, it makes perfect sense to use whatever tools you enjoy most, regardless of their lightfast rating.

Advertisement
How is Lightfastness Measured?
There are three main ways to measure how much a colour fades over time:
Blue Wool Scale
– An industry standard using blue-dyed wool strips that fade at different intervals. My testing is based on this method.
ASTM D6901
– A lab-based test for coloured pencils only, using controlled light exposure. Not suitable for markers.
Manufacturer Ratings
– Internal tests done by brands, which can vary in accuracy.
I talk about more of these in more detail in
this blog post.

data.title: The chemical secrets that help keep honey fresh for so long
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 蜂蜜因其特殊的化学性质和制作过程，具有极强的抗变质能力。蜜蜂在酿蜜过程中，通过去除花蜜中的水分并使用酶提高酸度，使得蜂蜜的含水量降至15%-18%，同时糖分高度浓缩。这种低水分高糖的环境抑制了微生物的生长。密封的蜂蜜限制了氧气接触，进一步防止变质。虽然蜂蜜可能会结晶，但在适当保存下不会变质。然而，开封后接触空气和污染物可能导致变质。这种抗腐能力使得蜂蜜被视为一种“神奇”的食品，类似于现代食品科学中的“低水分活性”保存法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：蜂蜜为何能长时间保持新鲜及其相关特性

不同观点：
• **Jun8的观点**：通过降低水分活度（aw），Nutella和蜂蜜等食品能够在不冷藏的情况下长时间保持新鲜。Nutella的aw约为0.4，蜂蜜的aw为0.5-0.6，而花生酱的aw为0.7，这些都使得它们能够较长时间保鲜。
• **YeGoblynQueenne的观点**：即使蜂蜜暴露在空气中并接触到细菌和湿气，它仍然不容易变质。基于个人经验，打开的蜂蜜罐即使放置多年也不会变质，虽然外观可能变得不吸引人。
• **bjelkeman-again的观点**：蜂蜜中常见的乳酸菌具有抗菌效果，能够抑制其他细菌的生长，这也是蜂蜜保持新鲜的原因之一。
• **cypherpunks01的观点**：蜂蜜中可能含有少量的肉毒杆菌，这种细菌会导致婴儿肉毒中毒，因此不建议给婴儿食用蜂蜜。
• **kragen的观点**：低水分活度和低pH值并不能完全解释蜂蜜惊人的保鲜能力。蜂蜜的保存性还与其含有葡萄糖氧化酶产生的葡萄糖酸和过氧化氢，以及甲基乙二醛等成分有关。

补充讨论：
• **__mharrison__的经验**：在急救培训中了解到蜂蜜可以帮助伤口更快愈合，并通过个人实验验证了这一说法。
• **RataNova的观点**：蜜蜂在数千年前就创造了一种生物化学保存系统，远早于人类建立食品科学实验室。
• **cryptonector的观点**：高糖浓度可以破坏简单生物的细胞，这也是蜂蜜能够保持新鲜的原因之一。
• **giantg2的观点**：蜂蜜保鲜的真正秘密在于其产生的高渗透压。
• **SeanDav的经验**：曾经养蜂，但因对蜂蜇过敏而不得不放弃。养蜂不仅有趣，还能对环境和食品生产做出贡献。
• **Daisywh的观点**：对是否可以将类似的自然保存原理应用于非食品保存感到好奇。
• **comrade1234的观点**：对渗透压的概念感兴趣，并表示会去阅读相关文章。
• **dartharva的观点**：提到LLM（大型语言模型）在处理心理健康问题时的不足，认为这可能与系统提示设置有关。
• **mhb的观点**：类似的情况也适用于巧克力。
• **montakaoh的提醒**：市场上有许多假蜂蜜，这些假蜂蜜的保存能力可能不如真正的蜂蜜，并提供了一个视频链接以供参考。

争议焦点：
• 蜂蜜保鲜的关键因素究竟是低水分活度、乳酸菌的抗菌效果，还是其他化学成分（如葡萄糖酸和甲基乙二醛）的作用。
• LLM在处理心理健康问题时的适当性及系统提示设置的影响。

44463429.article_content:
The chemical secrets that help keep honey fresh for so long
6 days ago
Share
Save
Veronique Greenwood
Share
Save
Getty Images
Honey is a natural sweetener, and bacteria loves to feast on sugar. But honey is remarkably resistant to spoilage. What's behind its ability to beat the bugs?
Most jarred delights have a limited shelf life – they're just one mucky spoon dip away from growing a luscious crop of mould or a thriving colony of bacteria. But there are certain foods with peculiar staying power, capable of staying edible for years.
Honey is one of these magical substances. In a sealed environment, while the golden stuff may crystallise, turning thick and chunky,
it will not go off
. This persistent ability to resist decay is down to honey's chemistry, and the way in which it is made.
When we say that food has spoiled, what we actually mean is that
something else
has got to it first, something microscopic. Bacteria, fungi, and moulds
are present
in at least low numbers in many foods, and a number of the procedures humans use to preserve food are designed to discourage these creatures consuming it.
Alamy
Honey may crystallise when it is in a sealed jar, but it does not go off (Credit: Alamy)
Many of these microorganisms tend to prefer moist conditions, higher (but not too high) temperatures, a mellow pH, and plenty of oxygen around to use in their metabolism. Dehydrating meat or fruit, then, deprives them of water. Cooking food to a high heat and then moving it into the fridge for storage first kills off many bugs and puts a damper on the growth of any left behind. Suspending food in a pickling mixture wards off all but the most acid-loving creatures. Sealing something in a jar limits the oxygen they have access to.
We are always fighting a losing battle against these organisms
Even food that's been put through a gauntlet of preservation procedures usually has a limited shelf life, as you might know if you have ever opened a jar of butterscotch sauce from the back of grandma's fridge, sealed in 1985, to find a thick carpet of fuzz within. (Don't ask me how I know.)
We are always fighting a losing battle against these organisms, and whether it's a whiff of vinegar that tells us the
Lactobacillus
has had its way with the orange juice, or black mould spots on the inside wall of the peanut butter jar, the signs of their presence are often unsubtle, and unavoidable.
But honey is an unusual case, and here is why. It's made by honeybees from flower nectar, and starts out as a warmish, watery, sugary fluid, the kind of thing that seems like it would be the purest bacteria bait. The bees
concentrate the nectar
on the way to the hive, removing some of the water, use enzymes to raise the acid content in the fluid discouraging some forms of microorganisms from growing, and break down the sugars into simpler ones, then decant the stuff into honeycomb chambers.
Getty Images
Sealing honey in jars adds to the purifying procedures bees carry out, which massively reduces the water content (Credit: Getty Images)
Next, they do something remarkable: they start to fan the
honey with their wings
. The fanning slowly evaporates the remaining water, like an oscillating fan evaporating sweat from your skin, so a substance that was once about
70% or 80% water
sees that number drop and drop and drop.
Fully ripened honey typically has a water content between about
15% and 18%
. In fact, the proportion of sugar molecules to water is so enormous that it would not be physically possible to dissolve that much sugar into that much water, without a process like the one honeybees use.
More like this:
•
Bee gold: Why honey is an insect superfood
•
How to make fruit and vegetables last longer
•
The food that could last 2,000 years
There is plenty of sugar there, and of course microorganisms would love to have a go at it. But with so little water – and the acidity providing an additional disincentive – they simply can't survive. Seal honey in a jar, to limit the availability of oxygen, and there's another barrier to growth.
This is a state known as "low water activity" among food scientists, and in fact, lowering a substance's water activity is a common trick to preserve processed foods. It is possible to keep
moist food from spoiling as long as the water molecules are tied up in interactions with salt or sugar
, for example.
This doesn't mean that honey can withstand all challenges to freshness. Once a jar of honey is open, its surface is being regularly exposed to the air, and dipping licked spoons in will bring bacteria and moisture that weren't there when the jar was sealed.
But take charge of the situation by adding water, add your own specially chosen microorganism, and you get
mead
– a type of spoilage that few would argue with on a hot day, sitting in the shade.

• **__mharrison__的经验**：在急救培训中了解到蜂蜜可以帮助伤口更快愈合，并通过个人实验验证了这一说法。
• **RataNova的观点**：蜜蜂在数千年前就创造了一种生物化学保存系统，远早于人类建立食品科学实验室。
• **cryptonector的观点**：高糖浓度可以破坏简单生物的细胞，这也是蜂蜜能够保持新鲜的原因之一。
• **giantg2的观点**：蜂蜜保鲜的真正秘密在于其产生的高渗透压。
• **SeanDav的经验**：曾经养蜂，但因对蜂蜇过敏而不得不放弃。养蜂不仅有趣，还能对环境和食品生产做出贡献。
• **Daisywh的观点**：对是否可以将类似的自然保存原理应用于非食品保存感到好奇。
• **comrade1234的观点**：对渗透压的概念感兴趣，并表示会去阅读相关文章。
• **dartharva的观点**：提到LLM（大型语言模型）在处理心理健康问题时的不足，认为这可能与系统提示设置有关。
• **mhb的观点**：类似的情况也适用于巧克力。
• **montakaoh的提醒**：市场上有许多假蜂蜜，这些假蜂蜜的保存能力可能不如真正的蜂蜜，并提供了一个视频链接以供参考。

争议焦点：
• 蜂蜜保鲜的关键因素究竟是低水分活度、乳酸菌的抗菌效果，还是其他化学成分（如葡萄糖酸和甲基乙二醛）的作用。
• LLM在处理心理健康问题时的适当性及系统提示设置的影响。

data.title: The Miyawaki Method of micro-forestry
data.author: zeristor
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了宫脇方法（Miyawaki Method）这一微型森林种植技术，该方法通过种植本地树种，在短时间内打造密集的小型森林，已在全球范围内受到广泛关注。文章探讨了宫脇方法的创始人宫脇昭博士的遗产，以及该方法在不同地区的应用实例，如横滨国立大学和温哥华的Strathcona公园。尽管宫脇方法在绿化爱好者和政府中颇受欢迎，但专业生态学家对其效果的评价较少。文章还引用了多篇相关文献和案例研究，讨论了该方法的成功和争议。最后，文章邀请读者支持相关播客，以获取更多内容。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Miyawaki植树法及其应用效果和相关生态问题

不同观点：
• **支持Miyawaki方法**：[lordswork]详细介绍了Miyawaki方法的关键步骤，如土壤有机质处理、混合种植本地植物、密集种植和覆盖。他认为这种方法能比传统方法更快地形成生物多样性丰富的森林。[zeristor]提到该方法在全球范围内受到广泛欢迎，但同时指出专业生态学家对其效果的评论较少。

• **方法的适用性有限**：[PaulHoule]指出，Miyawaki方法在某些生态系统中效果较好，但如果选错了植物材料或应用于不合适的生态系统，可能会失败，特别是在热带地区。[goda90]认为，虽然任何形式的造林都是好的，但不能忽视大型、连续森林生态系统的重要性，因为森林的片段化可能会威胁到某些物种的生存。

• **其他替代方法**：[shermantanktop]提到Crowther实验室的研究，指出一些植树项目可能被用于绿色洗白，且讨论了树木根系与地下生物群落的互动。[J7jKW2AAsgXhWm]分享了在伯克利的观察，认为虽然Miyawaki方法有其优点，但通过在公共空间增加树木和景观设计也能获得类似的好处，且这些方法可能更易实现和维护。

• **简要总结**：[contingencies]简要总结为“种植本地植物”。

争议焦点：Miyawaki方法的广泛适用性及其在不同生态系统中的效果。

Summary
The Miyawaki Method of micro-forestry is a viral sensation: sprouting tiny, dense, native tree cover in neighbourhoods all around the world. With the promise of afforestation at a revolutionary speed, this planting technique has become the darling of green-space enthusiasts, industry, and governments alike — yet few professional or academic ecologists have commented on its efficacy, or even seem to have heard of it!
In this episode, we debate the legacy of Dr. Akira Miyawaki: the man, the myth, and the method.

data.title: CU Randomness Beacon
data.author: wello
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于可验证随机性来源及其应用的讨论

不同观点：
• [grokgrok] 认为多个政府机构同步使用相同的随机源可能导致不良后果，例如同时收到陪审团义务、税务审计和征兵通知，暗示这种集中化的随机性管理存在潜在问题。

• [wuiheerfoj] 对可验证的量子随机性表示兴趣，并提到另一个使用传统加密技术的可验证随机性信标（drand.love），支持使用技术上更先进和可信的随机性来源。

• [Cshelton] 以幽默方式评论，提到使用实际事件（如Ralphie的跑步）作为真实随机性的来源，暗示对某些随机性来源的信任问题。

• [CaliforniaKarl] 关注API的兼容性问题，希望新的随机性信标能使用与NIST信标相同的API，以提高互操作性。

• [spelunker] 表示对随机性来源的物理原理感兴趣，特别是对不熟悉物理学的用户，提供了一个学习资源链接。

• [Octokat] 仅发表简短评论，无明确观点。

• [wslh] 推荐了解Twine Protocol，认为其在时间戳信任基础上创建的无共识层区块链可能有参考价值，暗示区块链技术在随机性应用中的潜力。

• [tonnydourado] 以幽默方式回应，无明确观点。

• [ribcage] 强烈反对依赖外部随机性网站，认为每台计算机都能生成随机性，质疑信任此类网站的必要性。

• [ntnsndr] 提出区块链技术的应用场景问题，暗示对区块链技术在随机性领域应用的兴趣或质疑。

补充讨论：
- 不同评论者对随机性来源的信任和技术实现有不同看法，部分关注具体技术实现和兼容性，部分则对实际应用场景和信任问题提出质疑。
- 评论中涉及的技术包括量子随机性、传统加密技术和区块链技术，显示出对多种技术路径的探讨。
- 争议的焦点在于是否应信任第三方提供的随机性来源以及如何在实际应用中实现随机性的可验证性和安全性。

data.title: Why are there still 7 continents?
data.author: jppope
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了“大陆”的定义以及当前不同的大陆划分模型，如美国/西欧的7大洲模型、联合国的6大洲模型、俄罗斯的6大洲模型等，指出这些模型的划分标准并不一致且存在随意性。作者认为，欧洲被视为一个大陆更多是历史和文化因素所致，而非地理或地质上的合理性。作者提出一个基于地质特征、面积、隔离程度和人口的更一致的大陆划分标准，认为大陆应作为一种组织世界的工具，而不仅仅是历史遗留的概念。文章最后列举了一些明确应被视为大陆的区域，如亚洲、非洲、北美洲和南美洲，并对南极洲和澳大利亚是否应被视为大陆提出了看法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于“大陆”定义和分类标准的争议及其合理性

不同观点：
• MarkusQ认为当前的定义比较宽松，甚至有人可能试图将冥王星称为大陆，暗示对大陆定义的不严谨。
• TrnsltLife提到法国教授5个大陆的体系，并分享了关于南北美洲分类的讨论，提到有人认为将南北美洲分开是种族主义，但最终通过解释解决了误解。
• JdeBP指出人们对大陆定义的荒谬性，提到有人将与自己生活区域有地理连接的地方称为“大陆”，并推荐了一个质疑7大洲教条的YouTube视频。
• theandrewbailey支持6大洲的欧亚模型，并调侃称将开始把欧洲称为次大陆。
• littlekey质疑“大陆”这一分类是否有用，提出这个概念的价值问题。
• kazinatory幽默地提到“incontinent”（失禁）的定义也很宽松，可能是对当前大陆定义随意性的调侃。
• gus_massa质疑6大洲模型中将欧洲单独列出的必要性。
• teruakohatu提到新西兰有可能声称拥有一个“大陆”（西兰洲），但并不打算真正提出外交主张。
• madcaptenor讽刺地说欧洲是大陆因为欧洲人发明了大陆的概念。
• OgsyedIE讨论了地质学中的克拉通（craton）概念，并指出根据维基百科上对克拉通的列表，有些大陆如格陵兰被忽略，质疑大陆定义的技术标准。
• fuzzfactor回应了关于第八大洲的问题，幽默地认为如果出现第八大洲将是一个重大事件。

补充讨论：
- 大陆定义的文化差异：法国与美国在教授大陆分类上的不同。
- 地质学角度对大陆定义的质疑：克拉通与大陆的关系。
- 大陆分类在实际地理和政治中的潜在争议：如新西兰对西兰洲的主张。
- 对大陆分类实用性的根本质疑：是否有必要继续使用这一概念。

44492888.article_content:
We've been teaching my kids about "the continents" and to the credit of my kid he asked me "what makes a continent?" Off the top of my head I didn't know precisely where the definition came from. I did however love the fact that my 5 year old has enough sense to ask why this thing is a thing. So I looked it up. Turns out the whole thing makes as much sense as a football bat.
Even after reading up on it I still can't figure out for the life of me why we have 7 continents. To be fair, when I say "we" I am talking about the American/ Western European model. There are other
models
, but they also feel pretty silly. Here are the most common continent models right now:
6 continents (The United Nations): Africa, Asia, Europe, "Americas", Antartica, Australia. This is taught mostly in Greece and Latin America according to wikipedia
6 continents (Russia/ Eastern Europe): Africa, Eurasia, Europe, North America, South America, Antartica, Australia
5 continent model: the 6 (UN) continent model but it just removes Antartica due to the fact that people don't live there.
5 continent model: A different 5 continent model just kinda says fuck it and starts combining things randomly (like Africa and Europe?)
4 continent model: cause why not?
And there is an 8 content model which arbitrarily includes Zealandia, a submerged landmass that is large, but its also only like ~700,000 square miles bigger than the indian sub-continent, has no people, isn't a tectonic plate.
Oddly,
the only pre-existing one that sort of makes sense to me is the 6-continent geological/ Russian model
. They have Africa, Eurasia, North America, South America, Antartica, and Austrailia. This is roughly a geological model. Presumably, they are the largest landmasses on tetonic plates. (See tectonic image below)
When I look at the status quo,
the obvious problem is Europe calling themselves a continent
, which is clearly a historic/ cultural legacy situation. Europe is on a contigous plate with Asia, its a relatively small landmass. If you are going to make Europe a continent and keep some level of intellectual consistency you definitely need to add the Indian subcontinent, and probably the Arabian Peninsula/ Greenland.
I think the Europeans are just using good old fashioned marketing by making all the important maps show Europe as larger than it really is...
When I look at the overall situation though,
I really don't hate Europe as a continent.
It's geographically separated from the other population centers on its tectonic plate, has a large enough landmass, and a large population.
What are continents anyway?
I think all the definitions kind of suck so lets say continents are an organizational tool that help to break down the world into more manageable pieces. By that definition the current models still suck, BUT we can likely build a more consistent model.
Building a better rubric
I get that arguing about the continents is about as useful as turn signals on a bmw. but here's my "I can build a bikeshed" model for you. Feel free to tell me its trash or improve it.
Geology
Separate geologic features such as tectonic plates, continental shelf, make up of the landmass.
Size
At a certain point the size of the landmass and divisibility is really what we're talking about here.
Distance and separation
How "distinct" is the thing. Kansas is a hard sell, but Madagascar is pretty darn separate.
Population
Since the continental model is mostly for organizing things, the population is actually a useful feature.
Definitely Continents
Asia
1-3 tectonic plates
Largest single landmass with or without Europe being included.
Without Europe - 44,579,000 km2 (17,212,000 sq mi)
With Europe -  55,000,000 km2 (21,000,000 sq mi)
Separated from other contents (except potentially for Europe) by oceans. or narrow strips of land.
4,694,576,167 people or 5.4 billion (with Europe)
Africa
Contains 2 tectonic plates with the majority being on one tectonic plate
Second largest landmass
30,370,000 km2 (11,730,000 sq mi)
Completely separated from other continents by water
1,393,676,444 people
North America
1 tectonic plate

Basically separated from other continents by water
592,296,233 people
South America
1 techonic plate
4th largest landmass
17,840,000 km2 (6,890,000 sq mi)
Basically separated from other continents by water
434,254,119 people
Probably Continents
Antartica
1 tectonic plate
5th largest landmass
14,200,000 km2 (5,500,000 sq mi)
Completely separated from other continents by oceans
5100 people (summer)
So the population element is really the only point of contention. Does a continent need a population? To me it feels like it shouldn't. When we nuke ourselves into a nuclear winter Antartica will still be just chillin'... Continents should be able to out last people.

44492888.article_summary: 本文讨论了“大陆”的定义以及当前不同的大陆划分模型，如美国/西欧的7大洲模型、联合国的6大洲模型、俄罗斯的6大洲模型等，指出这些模型的划分标准并不一致且存在随意性。作者认为，欧洲被视为一个大陆更多是历史和文化因素所致，而非地理或地质上的合理性。作者提出一个基于地质特征、面积、隔离程度和人口的更一致的大陆划分标准，认为大陆应作为一种组织世界的工具，而不仅仅是历史遗留的概念。文章最后列举了一些明确应被视为大陆的区域，如亚洲、非洲、北美洲和南美洲，并对南极洲和澳大利亚是否应被视为大陆提出了看法。

data.author: ArmageddonIt
data.article_summary: 这篇文章由史蒂夫·布兰克于2025年7月8日发布，题为《无视颠覆的CEO们如何错失未来》。文章引用海明威的话引出主题，讨论了面对颠覆性技术时企业如何逐渐走向破产。以20世纪初的美国为例，当时有超过4000家马车制造商，但随着汽车这一颠覆性技术的出现，只有一家公司幸存。文章强调了领导者在面对技术变革时必须适应或面临淘汰，并通过历史案例说明了企业在颠覆性技术面前失败或成功的经验教训。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI技术的发展及其对企业和社会的深远影响

不同观点：
• BrenBarn：认为AI带来的最大问题不是技术变革本身，而是道德和伦理问题，如隐私、创造力、著作权和不平等。AI只是放大了这些问题，而不是其根本原因。
• jampa：指出当前的AI热潮可能偏离了实际需求，过分关注表面的聊天机器人和简单应用，而忽视了AI在底层用户赋能方面的深层次应用。引用Jeff Bezos 2016年的观点，AI的最佳应用是在背后默默支持用户。
• barrysaunders：认为预测未来的技术趋势非常困难，历史上许多公司因追逐技术潮流而失败的例子不在少数，AI hype可能也会有类似的结果。
• analog31：通过个人经历讽刺企业对“颠覆”概念的盲目追随，书架上满是关于“颠覆”的书籍。
• habosa：认为 carriage 公司转型汽车制造未必会成功，大多数可能会生产出劣质产品，当前企业盲目追求“AI公司”标签可能导致平庸化。
• danbruc：认为当前的大型语言模型可能会成为技术发展的死胡同，AI的真正突破还需要新的基础理论。大型语言模型可能会作为用户界面或语言处理工具存在，但不会带来根本性变革。
• keeda：指出AI对知识工作的颠覆性影响，且这种现象可能没有历史可比性，企业需要认识到这种变化并适应，但目前似乎所有行业都在试图将AI塞进他们的产品中。
• nuker：通过历史人物的失败例子表达对未来的悲观看法。
• kylecazar：认为当前企业过于追逐AI潮流，忽视了基本功。
• johncole：认为当前CEO们因为动机问题夸大了AI对人类的替代作用，与历史上的技术变革不同。
• crossroadsguy：从个人经历出发，认为停留在舒适区和拒绝接受变化是人们错过技术潮流的原因。
• GianFabien：认为VC引入的职业经理人往往缺乏长远眼光，AI的需求可能没有普遍到让所有企业都需要转型，许多AI应用未必是大众需求的。
• anovikov：认为企业如果核心业务面临过时，转型成功的可能性很小，即使预见到趋势。
• dmbche：质疑文章中的历史案例是否真的能作为预测未来的教训，还是仅仅是幸存者偏差。
• burnt-resistor：通过家族历史展示从 carriage 到汽车的转型，反映技术变革的现实。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于AI是否真的会带来根本性变革，还是只是技术潮流的一部分，最终会回归理性。
- 另一个值得注意的讨论点是历史案例的适用性，是否真的能指导未来技术趋势的判断，还是仅仅为幸存者偏差。
- 企业盲目追求AI转型是否会导致资源错配和平庸化也是一个重要讨论点。

data.title: Memstop: Use LD_PRELOAD to delay process execution when low on memory
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: Memstop是一个轻量级工具，通过LD_PRELOAD机制监控系统内存，在可用内存达到设定百分比前延迟程序执行，以防止内存耗尽导致的系统崩溃。它适用于并行构建系统、批处理系统和高内存应用。Memstop从`/proc/meminfo`读取内存信息，计算所需内存百分比（默认10%），并在满足条件后允许程序继续执行。安装和使用需要GCC编译器和Linux系统，通过设置环境变量（如`MEMSTOP_PERBENT`和`MEMSTOP_VERBOSE`）进行配置。该项目使用GPL-3.0许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何在Android和Linux系统中有效管理内存使用，避免系统因内存不足而崩溃或变慢。具体讨论了内存管理的技术细节、调度机制的改进建议以及工具的使用。

不同观点：
• [AnotherGoodName] 提出了一种针对Android系统的内存管理“黑客”方法，通过生成新进程并捕获UNIX信号来避免系统弹出内存不足的通知，从而允许应用在低端设备上运行内存密集型任务。这种方法利用了Android的Low Memory Killer (LMK) 机制，通过手动触发内存失败来释放资源。

• [marcodiego] 则提出了对内存感知调度器的思考，建议系统对那些导致内存紧张的进程进行惩罚（如降低CPU时间），以避免系统因单个进程而变慢甚至崩溃。他还回顾了过去在能量感知调度方面的努力，认为类似的方法可以应用于内存管理。

• [meatmanek] 对使用LD_PRELOAD实现内存管理的方法提出疑问，认为直接使用命令行包装器可能更简单，并推测LD_PRELOAD的优势在于通过环境变量更容易集成到现有构建系统中。

• [nialv7] 认为没有必要使用复杂的方法，建议使用cgroup限制进程内存，并指出延迟或暂停进程可能导致无法释放内存，从而引发问题。

• [rini17] 关注设计哲学和内存指标（如RSS或虚拟内存），并建议通过添加swap空间来存储暂停的进程，同时警告可能出现死锁的情况。

• [d00mB0t] 对使用LD_PRELOAD的安全性提出关注，但总体上支持这种方法，并呼吁更多类似工具用于平行计算。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于不同方法的实用性和安全性。例如，LD_PRELOAD方法虽然灵活，但可能引入安全风险。
- 关于内存感知调度器的讨论，虽然有理论上的优点，但缺乏具体实现或失败案例的分析。

Memstop
A lightweight
LD_PRELOAD
shared object that delays process execution when system memory is critically low. Memstop monitors available memory and waits until a configurable percentage of memory becomes available before allowing the application to start.
Purpose
Memstop is designed to prevent crashes caused by memory exhaustion in parallel processing systems. It can be particularly useful in:
Parallel build systems (like
make -j
) where you want to prevent the build from failing due to the OOM (out-of-memory) killer
Batch processing systems where you want to ensure adequate memory before starting jobs
High-memory applications that might crash the system if started when memory is low
How It Works
When loaded as a shared object (via
LD_PRELOAD
), memstop automatically runs before your application's and all subprocesses'
main()
functions. It:
Reads system memory information from
/proc/meminfo
Calculates the required available memory percentage (default: 10%)
Waits until the specified percentage of memory is available
Releases control to your application once memory requirements are met
Build
Prerequisites
GCC compiler
Linux system with
/proc/meminfo
support
Make
Building from Source
#
Build the shared library
make
#
The build creates memstop.so
Install
System-wide Installation
#
Install to /usr/local/lib (requires root privileges)
sudo make install
Manual Installation
#
Copy to a directory in your library path
cp memstop.so /path/to/your/lib/directory
Usage
Basic Usage
Use
LD_PRELOAD
to load memstop before running your build process:
LD_PRELOAD=/usr/local/lib/memstop.so make -j
Configuration
Memstop is configured using environment variables:
MEMSTOP_PERCENT
Sets the percentage of total memory that must be available before allowing execution.
#
Require 20% of total memory to be available before make can spawn a task
MEMSTOP_PERCENT=20 LD_PRELOAD=/usr/local/lib/memstop.so make -j
#
Require 5% of total memory to be available
MEMSTOP_PERCENT=5 LD_PRELOAD=/usr/local/lib/memstop.so make -j
Default
: 10
Range
: 0-100
MEMSTOP_VERBOSE
Enables verbose output showing memory statistics and blocking status.
#
Enable verbose mode
MEMSTOP_VERBOSE=1 LD_PRELOAD=/usr/local/lib/memstop.so your_application
When enabled, memstop outputs to stderr:
Current memory statistics (required %, available %, MB available/total)
Hold notifications when delaying execution
Release notifications when allowing execution to continue
Warning:
Verbose mode can interfere with normal process execution and
should
normally be disabled
.
Sample Output
With
MEMSTOP_VERBOSE=1
:
==== memstop: 10% required, 15% available (1234 MB / 8192 MB) ====
If memory is insufficient:
==== memstop: 10% required, 5% available (410 MB / 8192 MB) ====
==== memstop hold ====
(after enough memory becomes available)
==== memstop release ====

data.title: Dynamical origin of Theia, the last giant impactor on Earth
data.author: bikenaga
data.article_summary: 这篇文章通过动力学模拟研究地球最后的巨型撞击者——Theia的起源。模拟从类地行星形成标准模型开始，包含行星胚胎和星子群，以及被木星向内散射的碳质（CC）物质。结果表明，该模型能解释地球和火星的质量与轨道、地球的CC物质比例、火星较低的CC比例、月球形成撞击的时间以及后期非碳质（NC）物质的增加。为使模拟成立，散射的CC物体总质量需为0.2-0.3地球质量，胚胎与星子质量比至少为8，CC胚胎质量在0.01-0.05地球质量之间。模拟显示，Theia有约50%的概率是纯CC胚胎或先前吸收了CC胚胎的NC胚胎，从而为宇宙化学研究提供了动力学验证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于地球历史上的巨型撞击事件及其可能的理论推演

不同观点：
• [nehal3m] 认为这是迄今为止最后一次巨大的撞击事件。该评论简单陈述了事件本身，并没有深入探讨其影响或背后的理论。

• [shadowgovt] 对该理论进行了详细解读，认为这是一个值得检验的假设。其主要观点是，通过模拟来验证假设是否与当前对太阳系形成的理解相矛盾是明智的做法。该评论强调了科学验证的必要性，并指出如果假设不与现有知识冲突，那么它是有价值的。

• [readthenotes1] 关注地球质量的变化，指出即使月球只有地球质量的1.2%，地球仍然因为撞击而变得更大。这表明该评论者更关注撞击事件对地球物理状态的直接影响。

• [echelon] 提出了一个富有想象力的观点，即如果在撞击前地球或Theia上已经演化出生命，尤其是智慧生命，那么这种生命将如何面对这样的灾难。该评论还进一步探讨了生命在宇宙中其他地方起源的可能性，甚至在没有行星或恒星的情况下，生命也可能在原始星际介质中形成，并播种整个宇宙。

补充讨论：
• [echelon] 引入了对智慧生命在撞击事件前存在的幻想性思考，尽管认为这种情况不太可能。同时，该评论还涉及了宇宙早期条件可能有利于生命起源的科学假设，并提出大多数外星生命可能具有相同的分子和手性特征，如果这些特征在星系形成之前就已经确定。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议点在于假设的合理性和科学验证的必要性。虽然[shadowgovt]认为验证假设是科学进步的重要步骤，但[echelon]则通过幻想性场景提出了对生命起源和智慧生命存在时间的质疑，这涉及到对现有科学理解的挑战和扩展。

Title:
Dynamical origin of Theia, the last giant impactor on Earth
Authors:
Duarte Branco
,
Sean N. Raymond
,
Pedro Machado
View a PDF of the paper titled Dynamical origin of Theia, the last giant impactor on Earth, by Duarte Branco and 2 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Cosmochemical studies have proposed that Earth accreted roughly 5-10% of its mass from carbonaceous (CC) material, with a large fraction delivered late via its final impactor, Theia (the Moon-forming impactor). Here, we evaluate this idea using dynamical simulations of terrestrial planet formation, starting from a standard setup with a population of planetary embryos and planetesimals laid out in a ring centered between Venus and Earth's orbits, and also including a population of CC planetesimals and planetary embryos scattered inward by Jupiter. We find that this scenario can match a large number of constraints, including i) the terrestrial planets' masses and orbits; ii) the CC mass fraction of Earth; iii) the much lower CC mass fraction of Mars, as long as Mars only accreted CC planetesimals (but no CC embryos); iv) the timing of the last giant (Moon-forming) impact; and v) a late accretion phase dominated by non-carbonaceous (NC) bodies. For this scenario to work, the total mass in scattered CC objects must have been ~ 0.2 - 0.3 M$_{\oplus}$ , with an embryo-to-planetesimal mass ratio of at least 8, and CC embryos in the ~ 0.01 - 0.05 M$_{\oplus}$ mass range. In that case, our simulations show there are roughly 50-50 odds of Earth's last giant impactor (Theia) having been a carbonaceous object - either a pure CC embryo or an NC embryo that previously accreted a CC embryo. Our simulations thus provide dynamical validation of cosmochemical studies.

data.title: Breaking Git with a carriage return and cloning RCE
data.author: dgl
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了CVE-2025-48384漏洞，该漏洞影响Unix类平台上的Git。当用户使用`git clone --recursive`克隆不受信任的代码库时，可能导致远程代码执行。漏洞源于Git处理配置文件时对回车符（CR）和换行符（LF）的处理不当。Git的配置格式支持DOS换行符（CR+LF），但在特定情况下，Git会错误地处理以回车符结尾的值，可能导致控制字符被引入文件路径中。攻击者可以利用此漏洞，在子模块路径中插入恶意控制字符，从而在克隆过程中执行任意代码。为避免此问题，用户应更新到Git的修复版本，并谨慎处理不受信任的代码库。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Git版本发布时间线、安全漏洞（CVE-2025-48386等）的影响及修复情况、技术细节和潜在解决方案

不同观点：
• [capitol_] 对Git 2.50.1版本的发布时间感到困惑，因为该版本标记日期是2025-06-16，但大多数发行版尚未修复该漏洞。质疑Git是否回溯了发布日期。
• [armchairhacker] 讨论了漏洞如何导致远程代码执行（RCE），指出通过恶意Git钩子可以利用该漏洞，并提供了与CVE-2024-32002漏洞的关联及技术细节。
• [10000truths] 认为使用自定义DSL进行配置是一个大问题，缺乏正式的语法规范可能导致解析差异，建议使用单一事实来源生成所有依赖项。
• [acheong08] 成功复现了该问题并分享了相关链接，提到Arch Linux尚未更新Git版本，预计大多数人升级需要时间。
• [JdeBP] 引用了历史文献和分析，指出该问题与早期关于解析和引用的讨论相关，强调需要反复学习20世纪的教训。

44502330.article_content:
CVE-2025-48384: Breaking git with a carriage return and cloning RCE
tl;dr:
On Unix-like platforms, if you use
git clone --recursive
on an
untrusted repo, it could achieve remote code execution. Update to a
fixed
version
of git and other software that embeds Git (including GitHub Desktop).
If you've ever used an old mechanical typewriter, you know that when you get to
the end of the line there's a physical action to to get back to the start of
the line. Sometimes this was done through an actual lever on the typewriter,
later models had a button. Because this action — the
carriage
return
— was distinct from the
line feed, it has its own character. In ASCII this is the character known as
"Carriage Return", represented as "␍", character number 13. The "↵" icon, as
often seen on the "Enter" or "Return" key on a modern keyboard encodes this
action, along with the action of moving to the next line, known as "Line Feed"
(␊).
An Olympia SM9 with a carriage return lever. Via
classictypewriter.com
.
This legacy from the very early days of communications (carriage return was
introduced by the
Murray
code
in 1901!) is still
something we have to deal with. Unix attempted to simplify this by using just
LF (a "\n" in C-string terms) to separate lines, but Windows and various
Internet protocols use both CR+LF (a "\r\n" in C-string terms).
Why am I talking about
this
?
git has a simple .ini style configuration format, that looks like this:
[section]
key = value
If this was just used in the user’s configuration files there wouldn’t be a
concern about the formats that are accepted. However this configuration format
is also used in the
.gitmodules
file, which is a file that is checked into
the git repository that tracks submodules.
The format supports DOS line endings. It handles this in the fairly obvious way
of stripping them when it reads lines, below is the function get_next_char in
config.c:
static int get_next_char(struct config_source *cs)
{
int c = cs->do_fgetc(cs);
if (c == '\r') {
/* DOS like systems */
c = cs->do_fgetc(cs);
if (c != '\n') {
if (c != EOF)
cs->do_ungetc(c, cs);
c = '\r';
}
}
The
cs->do_fgetc
call is nearly equivalent to the standard C function
fgetc()
, so even without knowledge of git's particular functions this is
quite understandable.
It boils down to: If the character is a carriage return (
\r
), then look at
the next character, if it is a line feed (
\n
), just return a line feed (and
eat the carriage return). If however the next character isn’t a line feed,
return a carriage return (
\r
) and put the next character back (
ungetc
), so
it is returned next time.
The key thing to understand here is that this is done per line. So if for some
reason a line happens to end with a CR, it will be stripped, regardless of the
overall format of the file.
In addition to the code to read the configuration, git can also write
configuration files, for example when the user uses
git config
to set a
configuration value, it will use the code below to write
key = value
pairs
out to the file.
static ssize_t write_pair(int fd, const char *key, const char *value, [...]
{
[...]
/*
* Check to see if the value needs to be surrounded with a dq pair.
* Note that problematic characters are always backslash-quoted; this
* check is about not losing leading or trailing SP and strings that
* follow beginning-of-comment characters (i.e. ';' and '#') by the
* configuration parser.
*/
if (value[0] == ' ')
quote = "\"";
for (i = 0; value[i]; i++)
if (value[i] == ';' || value[i] == '#')
quote = "\"";
if (i && value[i - 1] == ' ')
quote = "\"";
strbuf_addf(&sb, "\t%s = %s", key + store->baselen + 1, quote);
The actual bug is in the interaction of the above get_next_char function with
this code. Elsewhere in the configuration reading code git supports quoted
strings, using double quotes. However, when it writes a value back out to the
configuration file, it will quote it only if it contains spaces in certain
positions, or a
;
or
#
anywhere. This means when it later reads the value
write_pair
wrote to the configuration file back, it can be tricked to drop a
final
\r
off the value.
So, if we have a file with
key = "foo^M"
, when it's written out again it
becomes
key = foo^M
(where
^M
is the literal CR character).
As I alluded to already,
.gitmodules
is untrusted, so if we can confuse the
config parser, maybe that’s enough to confuse the code that handles submodules
within git?
On Unix based systems (not Windows), it is possible to have control characters
in filenames, so a path entry like the following in
.gitmodules
will attempt
to check out the module into a directory named with a control character in its
name.
[submodule "foo"]
path = "foo^M"
However when this is written out by git’s configuration code to
.git/modules/foo/config
, it will look something like this:
[core]
workdir = ../../../foo^M
The validation has already happened against the untrusted path that was read
from
.gitmodules
. This means the path then essentially changes
44502330.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了CVE-2025-48384漏洞，该漏洞影响Unix类平台上的Git。当用户使用`git clone --recursive`克隆不受信任的代码库时，可能导致远程代码执行。漏洞源于Git处理配置文件时对回车符（CR）和换行符（LF）的处理不当。Git的配置格式支持DOS换行符（CR+LF），但在特定情况下，Git会错误地处理以回车符结尾的值，可能导致控制字符被引入文件路径中。攻击者可以利用此漏洞，在子模块路径中插入恶意控制字符，从而在克隆过程中执行任意代码。为避免此问题，用户应更新到Git的修复版本，并谨慎处理不受信任的代码库。

data.article_summary: Radium是一款具有创新界面的音乐编辑器，相较于钢琴卷帘界面，其编辑速度更快，屏幕可容纳更多音乐数据。与追踪器界面相比，它支持图形化编辑音符位置和效果，提供更多垂直空间和更好的音乐数据可视化。Radium也是一款数字音频工作站（DAW），支持录音、编辑和混音，兼具文本编辑功能。自1999年开始开发，现已支持Linux、Windows和Mac。其功能包括多轨音频和MIDI、自动化参数、颗粒合成、平滑滚动、可选钢琴卷帘、无损变更缩放、微调音高、脚本编写、多核支持、无限撤销/重做等。Radium为开源软件，并提供Pure Data和Faust环境，支持多种插件格式。用户可以通过订阅支持其开发并获取优先更新。

Radium - The Music Editor
Home
Info
Download
Community
Forum
Compressor
About Radium
Radium is a music editor with a new type of interface.
Compared to the
piano roll interface
,
editing is quicker
and
more musical data fits on the screen
.
(Radium has a piano roll as well.)
Compared to the
tracker interface
,
note positions and effects can be edited graphically
. Graphical editing provides
more vertical space
and gives a
better visualization of musical data
.
(Everything can also be edited by text, like in a normal tracker, combining the best of two worlds.)
Radium is also a
Digitial Audio Workstation
(DAWg), which can be used to record, edit, and mix audio.
However, despite its unusual appearance, it's a design goal for Radium to be
straightforward to use, and easy to learn
.
It should not be harder to learn Radium than any tracker or most MIDI sequencers.
Users accustomed to trackers might use more time adjusting to the interface.
History
The development of Radium started in 1999 based on ideas developed 1997-1999 while extending the Octamed tracker on the Amiga.
The first public version of Radium was released in 2000.
Since then, Radium has been ported to Linux, Windows, and Mac.
Today, Radium is probably the worlds largest and most advanced tracker-like music editor.
Some of the features
Audio and MIDI multitracker
Automate pitch, velocity, effects, and tempo.
Granular synthesis
Smooth scrolling
Optional piano roll
Tickless
Global swing, and swing-per-track
Modular mixer and/or mixer strips
MIDI sequencing
Hard drive audio recording and playback
AU, LADSPA, LV2, VST, and VST3 plugins
(More than 100 LADSPA plugins are included)
Several built-in effects and instruments
(virtual instruments, multiband compressor, modulators, etc.)
Pure Data
embedded.
(Linux only for now)
Includes a
Faust
audio DSP development environment
Frame-accurately synchronize playback to e.g.
Ardour
,
Bitwig
, or
MASCHINE
.
Graphical zoom
Non-destructive changable Lines Per Beat ("Line Zoom").
Microtonality
Scripting in Python or Scheme.
Plugin delay compensation applied to all parts of the audio graph
Multicore support
Unlimited undo/redo
Open source with a straightforward and easy to use build system (no CMake or IDEs).
Quick start
Load a demo song from the File menu.
Play by pressing space.
Add a new note to the editor by pressing a key on the computer keyboard. Change octave with F1 and F2.
(Or record from MIDI input)
Look at the
manual.

data.author: kashifr
data.article_summary: SmolLM3是一款小型、多语言、支持长上下文推理的30亿参数语言模型，性能超越Llama-3.2-3B和Qwen2.5-3B，并可与40亿参数模型竞争。该模型支持6种语言，采用Transformer解码器架构，结合了Grouped Query Attention、NoPE等技术以提升效率和长上下文表现。通过三阶段预训练方法和混合推理模式，SmolLM3在多项任务中表现出色。其完整工程蓝图和训练方法已在GitHub上发布，包括架构细节、数据混合策略和训练配置，为开发者提供了详细的指导。模型训练使用了384块H100 GPU，耗时24天。

Small language models are becoming increasingly important as users seek capable models that can be deployed efficiently. The community has produced a fascinating range of capable small models, each pushing the boundaries of what's possible at this scale. With SmolLM3, we're excited to contribute a new competitive fully open 3B model:
Base model:
https://hf.co/HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM3-3B-Base
Instruct and reasoning model:
https://hf.co/HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM3-3B
SmolLM3 sits in the efficiency sweet spot.
Our 3B model outperforms Llama-3.2-3B and Qwen2.5-3B while staying competitive with larger 4B alternatives (Qwen3 & Gemma3). Beyond the performance numbers, we're sharing exactly how we built it using public datasets and training frameworks.
Model summary:
3B model
trained on 11T tokens, SoTA at the 3B scale and competitive with 4B models
Instruct model
with
dual mode reasoning,
supporting
think
/
no_think
modes
Multilingual support
for 6 languages: English, French, Spanish, German, Italian, and Portuguese
Long context
up to 128k with NoPE and using YaRN
The complete recipe:
We're releasing SmolLM3 with our engineering blueprint. It includes architecture details, exact data mixtures showing how we progressively boost performance across domains in a three-stage pretraining approach, and the methodology for building a hybrid reasoning model. Usually, achieving these results would require months of reverse engineering. Instead, we're providing the full methodology.
Whether you're building your own models or want to understand what drives performance at this scale, this blueprint shows the engineering story behind competitive 3B performance.
Let’s have a look at the pretraining stage.
Pretraining
SmolLM3 both changed the architecture and data mixture over its predecessors. Let’s have a look at the architecture and training configurations first!
Architecture and training details
SmolLM3 follows a transformer decoder architecture with tied embedding similar to SmolLM2, building on Llama architecture with some key modifications optimized for efficiency and long context performance.
Grouped Query Attention (GQA):
We replaced multi-head attention with grouped-query attention using 4 groups. Our ablations on a 3B model trained with 100B tokens from
FineWeb-Edu
showed that GQA matches the performance of multi-head attention while significantly reducing the KV cache size during inference.
NoPE:
We implemented NoPE from "
RoPE to NoRoPE and Back Again: A New Hybrid Attention Strategy
" (Yang et al., 2025), selectively removing rotary position embeddings from every 4th layer. This approach improves long context performance without affecting short context capabilities, as confirmed by our ablations.
Intra-Document Masking:
During training, we use attention masking to ensure tokens from different documents in the same training sequence don't attend to each other. Similar to Llama 3, this helps with faster and more stable long context training while maintaining short context performance.
Training Stability:
Following OLMo 2, we remove weight decay from embedding layers to improve training stability. This modification contributed to more stable training dynamics, with embedding norms naturally stabilizing at healthier values during training without impacting overall performance in our ablations.
All these changes were validated through ablations using the same 3B architecture trained on 100B tokens from FineWeb-Edu, ensuring each modification either improved performance or maintained it while offering other benefits.
Training Configuration: We use a global batch size of 2.36M tokens with 4096 sequence length, a learning rate of 2e-4, and the AdamW optimizer (beta1: 0.9, beta2: 0.95) with weight decay of 0.1 and gradient clipping of 1. We use the WSD (Warmup-Stable-Decay) scheduler, with 2000  warmup steps, and a linear decay to 0 in the final 10% training steps. We use
nanotron
framework for the training,
datatrove
for data processing and
lighteval
for evaluation. The model was trained on 384 H100 GPUs for 24 days. You can see the distributed training setup in the following figure.

data.title: Taking over 60k spyware user accounts with SQL injection
data.author: mtlynch
data.article_summary: 本文描述了作者如何发现并利用一款名为Catwatchful的安卓间谍软件服务中的SQL注入漏洞，最终获取了超过6万个间谍用户账户的数据。作者首先通过注册一个免费试用账户，发现该服务同时在Firebase和一个自定义服务器上创建账户。在分析其流量后，作者注意到用户数据存储在Firebase中，难以直接攻击，但注册时涉及的另一个服务器（catwatchful.pink）存在SQL注入漏洞。通过利用该漏洞，作者成功获取了大量用户的敏感信息，揭示了该间谍软件在安全性上的重大缺陷。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对Catwatchful间谍软件的技术分析、法律问题及道德争议

不同观点：
• **[mtlynch]**: 通过sqlmap工具发现Catwatchful存在SQL注入漏洞，并指出该恶意软件开发者在处理Firebase时避免了一些更严重的漏洞，但仍在其他方面（如明文密码存储和未过滤的用户输入）犯下了低级错误。Firebase的使用减少了部分攻击面，但开发者依然存在明显的安全失误。

• **[gpm]**: 质疑Google Play Protect的有效性，指出TechCrunch文章中的矛盾之处：文章声称Google增加了保护措施，但展示的截图却显示需要关闭Google Play Protect。同时，对Firebase继续托管此类应用表示不满。

• **[ryanrasti]**: 对现代Android系统中如何实现无感知的手机监控表示惊讶和质疑，认为这与Android的安全模型目标相悖。

• **[bspammer]**: 对间谍软件开发者在拥有一定技术能力的情况下仍犯下基本的安全错误感到意外，例如明文存储密码和未处理的用户输入。

• **[JohnMakin]**: 分享了自己曾遭遇类似间谍软件感染的经历，认为这些服务极其不道德，并对研究者的温和态度表示不满。

• **[zero_k]**: 对一些工程师在处理恶意服务时的无力感表示愤怒，认为应更迅速地采取措施（如关闭系统）来应对这些不道德行为，并批评相关人员缺乏责任感和羞耻心。

• **[blueplanet200]**: 引用了sqlmap的使用条款，指出未经授权的攻击是非法的，并提醒注意法律责任，认为即使道德上合理，法律上仍可能面临后果。

• **[bluelightning2k]**: 质疑使用类似间谍软件的合法性，建议将相关数据库提交给FBI进行起诉，并指出立法盲点。

• **[esaym]**: 对间谍软件的实时照片和录音功能感到不安，认为其非常 creepy（令人毛骨悚然）。

• **[ceva]**: 认为从事恶意软件业务的人不会因为此类行为起诉他人，对研究者的行为表示支持。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Catwatchful的技术漏洞及其在法律和道德上的问题。
• 讨论中涉及的法律问题包括使用sqlmap等工具的合法性、间谍软件的合法性及相关法律盲点。
• 道德争议集中在间谍软件的不道德性及相关服务提供者的责任感。
• 对Google Play Protect和Firebase的有效性和责任也存在质疑。

Background
#
Recently I was looking through a database of known stalkerware services and found one I wasn’t familiar with:
Catwatchful
. It seemed to be a full-featured Android spy app, to actually be its own service as opposed to a millionth FlexiSpy reseller, and to offer a 3-day free trial. Aside from a boilerplate disclaimer to only use it with consent, it also pretty brazenly advertised itself as stalkerware in the FAQ:
Q: Can I monitor a phone without them knowing?
A: Yes, you can monitor a phone without them knowing with mobile phone monitoring software. The app is invisible and undetectable on the phone. It works in a hidden and stealth mode.
Apparently still unsatisfied, it boasted even further about “absolute stealth” in a list of features:
Catwatchful is invisible. It cannot be detected. It cannot be uninstalled. It cannot be stopped. It cannot be closed. Only you can access the information it collects.
Let’s see about that last part, shall we?
Part 0: Setup
#
I began by making a free trial account on the website. Interestingly, this triggered two separate POST requests:

catwatchful.pink
.
After registration and login, I get given an APK to download and install. From here, installation goes as usual for Android stalkerware: the app has me download and install another APK pre-configured with my account credentials. This app then asks for basically every permission on the system, guides me through uninstalling the original installer app, then runs in the background forever while disguising itself in the app drawer with a generic “Settings” icon.
Part 1: Recon
#
After installing the app and re-logging into the web interface, I’m presented with a control panel with which to spy on my test phone. Two things stand out to me here: first of all, the app works really well. A lot of stalkerware apps are half-broken, clearly built by gluing together various chunks of spaghetti code long abandoned by their original authors. Not so here - all these features work as advertised with minimal latency. The live photo and microphone options are particularly creepy, successfully taking a photo or recording and uploading it for me to view near-instantly on the control panel without giving the phone user the slightest sign that anything is amiss.
The only bug I found was in the sidebar counters (I did not in fact take 3002 screenshots while testing)

This is going to reduce our attack surface by a lot - nothing in Firebase is going to be IDORable or vulnerable to SQLI, and some quick testing eliminates any of the usual traps like open storage buckets or client-side service account credentials. We’re going to have to focus on that mysterious
catwatchful.pink
server I was also signed up on.

#

• **[blueplanet200]**: 引用了sqlmap的使用条款，指出未经授权的攻击是非法的，并提醒注意法律责任，认为即使道德上合理，法律上仍可能面临后果。

• **[bluelightning2k]**: 质疑使用类似间谍软件的合法性，建议将相关数据库提交给FBI进行起诉，并指出立法盲点。

• **[esaym]**: 对间谍软件的实时照片和录音功能感到不安，认为其非常 creepy（令人毛骨悚然）。

• **[ceva]**: 认为从事恶意软件业务的人不会因为此类行为起诉他人，对研究者的行为表示支持。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Catwatchful的技术漏洞及其在法律和道德上的问题。
• 讨论中涉及的法律问题包括使用sqlmap等工具的合法性、间谍软件的合法性及相关法律盲点。
• 道德争议集中在间谍软件的不道德性及相关服务提供者的责任感。
• 对Google Play Protect和Firebase的有效性和责任也存在质疑。

data.title: Brut: A New Web Framework for Ruby
data.author: onnnon
data.article_summary:
Brut是一个简约但功能齐全的Ruby web框架，不同于其他框架，它没有控制器、动词或资源，而是直接构建页面、表单和单一操作处理器。Brut注重低抽象和低仪式感，但并非像Sinatra那样的低级框架。它内置OpenTelemetry仪表盘、基于Sequel的数据访问层以及基于OptionParser的命令行应用。

Brut安装简便，支持Docker快速启动。其核心设计基于类和对象，避免了过多的include和动态方法。它统一了客户端和服务器端表单验证，并通过BrutJS提供自定义元素。使用esbuild处理CSS，无需PostCSS或SASS。

Brut默认设置良好实践，如内容安全策略和数据库非空约束。它使用RSpec进行测试，支持Phlex生成HTML，并避免使用YAML进行配置。Brut简化了开发，消除了不必要的抽象和辩论，让开发者专注于编写Ruby和HTML，享受构建web应用的过程。

接下来，作者将继续完善Brut并发布1.0版本。

主要讨论点：围绕新web框架Brut的评价和讨论，涉及技术实现、框架对比、许可证问题以及实际使用反馈。

不同观点：
• **框架设计和实现的看法**：
   - [rorylaitila] 支持以表单和页面为核心的设计，认为控制器被过度使用，主张通过框架更优雅地处理验证和交互，强调表单和视图的重要性。
   - [sarchertech] 提到可以使用更高级的函数式编程概念（如monad、代数数据类型等），但认为这些不是必须的，适合小项目或由高级开发者参与的项目。

• **与其他框架的对比**：
   - [freedomben] 认为Brut是Sinatra和Rails之间的良好折中，适合不需要Rails复杂的简单应用。
   - [hamzakc] 建议考虑Roda框架，暗示可能有其他更合适的选择。
   - [gavmor] 提到Brut的命名方式避免了资源路由的混淆问题，但同时也提出了新的潜在问题。

• **许可证问题的讨论**：
   - [ilvez] 对Brut的特殊许可证表示关注，质疑是否影响源码查看。
   - [wrs] 和 [cosmojg] 详细讨论了Brut的HIPPOCRATIC LICENSE的细节，特别是其对使用者商业行为的严格限制，[wrs] 还提到需要检查供应链的道德问题。

   - [heeton] 在尝试登录示例网站时遇到错误，表明实际使用中可能存在问题。

补充讨论：

   - [Lio] 提到David的《Sustainable Rails》一书，并表示对Brut完全采用Sorbet进行类型检查的兴趣，但担心可能违背渐进类型方法。

• **其他资源推荐**：
   - [Alifatisk] 提到Brut官网的介绍页面，提供了更多信息来源。

44502463.article_content:
Brut
aims to be a simple, yet fully-featured web framework for Ruby. It's different than other Ruby web frameworks.  Brut has no controllers, verbs, or resources. You build pages, forms, and single-action handlers. You write HTML, which is generated on the server. You can write all the JavaScript and CSS you want.
Hereâs a web page that tells you what time it is:
class
TimePage
<
AppPage
def
initialize
(
clock
:)
@clock
=
clock
end
def
page_template
header
do
h1
{
"Welcome to the Time Page!"
}
TimeTag
(
timestamp:
@clock
.
now
)
end
end
end
Brut is built around low-abstraction and low-ceremony, but is not low-level like Sinatra.  Itâs a web framework. Your Brut apps have builtin OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation, a
Sequel
-powered data access layer, and developer automation based on
OptionParser
-powered command-line apps.
Brut
can be installed right now, and you can build and run an
app in minutes. You donât even have to install Ruby.
> docker run \
-v "$PWD":"$PWD" \
-w "$PWD" \
-it \
thirdtank/mkbrut \
mkbrut my-new-app
> cd my-new-app
> dx/build && dx/start
> dx/exec bin/setup
> dx/exec bin/dev
# => localhost:6502 is waiting
Thereâs a full-fledged example app called
ADRs.cloud
you can run right now and see how it works.
What You Get
Brut has extensive documentation
, however these are some highlights:
Brutâs core design is around classes that are instantiated into objects, upon which methods are called.
No excessive
include
calls to create a massive blob of functions.
No Hashes of Whatever. Your session, flash, and form parameters are all actual classes and defined data types.
Minimal reliance of dynamically-defined methods or
method_missing
.  Almost every
method
has documentation
.
Brut leverages the modern Web Platform.
Client-side and server-side form validation is unified into one user experience.
BrutJS
is an ever-evolving
library
of autonomous custom elements AKA web components to progressively enhance your
HTML.
With
esbuild
, you can write regular CSS and have
it instantly packaged, minified, and hashed. No PostCSS, No SASS.
Brut sets up good practices by default.
Your app will have a reasonable content security policy.
Your database columns arenât null by default.
Your foreign keys will a) exist, b) be indexed, and c) not be nullable by
default.
Time, available through Brutâs
Clock
, is always timezone-aware.
Localization is there and is as easy as we can make it. We hope to make it easier.
Brut uses awesome Ruby gems
RSpec is how you write your tests. Brut includes custom matchers to make it
easier to focus on what your code should do.
Faker and FactoryBot will set up your test and dev data
Phlex generates your HTML. No, we wonât be supporting HAML.
Brut doesnât recreate configuration with YAML.
I18n uses the
i18n gem
, with translations
in a Ruby Hash
. No YAML.
Dynamic configuration is in the environment, managed in dev and test by
the
dotenv gem
. No YAML.
OK, the dev environmentâs
docker-compose.dx.yml
is YAML. But thatâs
it
.
YAML, not even
once
twice.
Brut doesnât create abstractions where none were needed.
Is this the index action of the widgets resource or the show action of the widget-list resource?
is a question you will never have to ask yourself or your team. The widgets page is called
WidgetsPage
and available at
/widgets
.
My
Widgets
class accesses the
WIDGETS
table, but it also has all the domain logic of a widget!
No it doesnât.
DB::Widget
gets your data.  You can make
Widget
do whatever you want. Heck, make a
WidgetService
for all we care!
What if our HTML had controllers but they were not the same as the controllers in our back-end?
There arenât any controllers. You donât want them, you donât have to make them.
What about monads or algebraic data types or currying or maybe having everything
be a
Proc
because
call
?!
You donât have to understand any part of that question.  But if you want your business logic to use functors, go for it. We wonât stop you.
WHY?!?!?!
I know, we can vibe away all the boilerplate required for Rails apps.  But how much fun is that?  How much do you enjoy setting up RSpec, again, in your new Rails app? How tired are you of changing the âfront end solutionâ every few years?  And arenât you just
tired
of debating where your business logic goes or if itâs OK to use HTTP
DELETE
(tunneled over a
_method
param in a
POST
) to archive a widget?
I know I am.
I want to have fun building web apps, which means I want write Ruby, use HTML, and leverage the browser. Do you know how awesome browsers are now?  Also, Ruby 3.4 is pretty great as well. Iâd like to use it.
What I
donât
want is endless flexibility, constant architectural decision-making, or pointless debates about stuff that doesnât matter.
I just want to have fun building web apps.
Next Steps
I will continue working
toward a 1.0 of Brut
, building web apps and enjoying the process.  I hope you will, too!

Fix Your Dev Environment for Good

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：一个新的协作播放列表项目引发的多方面讨论

不同观点：
• **支持并提出功能改进建议**：
  - andelink：建议整合更多流媒体平台（如Spotify、Apple Music），通过服务如Odesli过滤非音乐内容，提升用户体验。
  - JodieBenitez：肯定无需账户的优点，同时建议增加文件链接上传功能。
  - corny：希望在最后一首歌播放完后保持播放状态，并希望既有音频也有视频播放功能。
  - foresto：建议支持Shoutcast流媒体播放，以便用户通过常规音响系统收听。

• **开源与法律合规性**：
  - extraduder_ire：指出MIT许可证未在代码库中以文件形式明确列出，建议添加license.txt文件。

• **与类似项目的比较**：
  - nzoschke：分享自己开发的类似开源项目Jukelab，强调老式点唱机的设计。
  - Unai：提到另一个同名且功能类似的长期存在的Jukebox项目，询问是否有关联或仅为同名。

• **怀旧与情感反馈**：
  - Aeolun：怀念Grooveshark的epicpower小组，并分享相关链接。
  - jason_zig：回忆起曾经的JQBX项目。

• **公平性讨论**：
  - jp57：提出人们对“公平”的理解不同，指出有些人可能认为先到先得是公平的，而该项目似乎并未采用这种公平观。

• **娱乐场景应用**：
  - lovegrenoble：分享一个适用于桌上角色扮演游戏（TTRPG）会话的类似工具链接。

• **安全与版权问题**：
  - cdurth：指出项目可能涉及将视频上传至S3，警告可能导致YouTube API密钥被撤销和遭遇DMCA投诉。

• **项目背景与个人情感**：
  - noleary：对项目作为“减压项目”的背景表示赞赏。

补充讨论：
- 评论中多次提到希望整合更多流媒体平台，尤其是Spotify和Apple Music，以提升用户体验。
- 用户对“公平”的定义存在争议，尤其是关于播放顺序的公平性问题。
- 对版权问题的关注，尤其是视频内容和YouTube API的使用，提示项目可能面临的法律风险。
- 对项目开源和法律合规性的建议，反映出用户对开源项目透明性和合法性的重视。

data.title: GlobalFoundries to Acquire MIPS
data.author: mshockwave
data.article_summary: 2025年7月8日，格芯（GlobalFoundries）宣布收购MIPS，以增强其在人工智能和计算能力方面的布局。此次收购将扩展格芯的定制IP产品组合，特别是在RISC-V处理器IP和实时计算软件工具方面，应用于自动驾驶、工业自动化、数据中心和智能边缘等领域。MIPS近期推出了基于RISC-V的Atlas处理器IP系列及虚拟优化平台Atlas Explorer，旨在提升性能和效率。格芯表示，收购MIPS将增强其提供灵活的RISC-V开放平台解决方案的能力，并结合其制造技术，助力客户打造更高效的产品。MIPS将成为格芯旗下的独立运营业务，继续服务其客户。收购预计在2025年下半年完成。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MIPS和RISC-V在CPU架构市场中的发展及未来可能性

不同观点：
• somanyphotons认为，拥有旧晶圆厂和内部CPU设计团队的公司可能会通过低价策略争取低端市场的份额，并提出这是否是市场整合的开始，特别是针对RISC-V CPU IP供应商的财务状况。
• musicale指出，MIPS错失了很多机会，如果MIPS曾经真正开放架构，可能就不需要RISC-V了。MIPS在工具支持、硅实现、压缩指令格式、64位指令集以及从嵌入式系统到高性能计算的扩展方面有十多年的领先优势。
• stevefan1999以幽默的方式表达了对MIPS现状的惊讶，暗示AMD曾经有机会发展MIPS但未果。
• sloemoe引用了MIPS架构中的延迟槽概念，并惊讶于许多其他架构也使用这一概念。
• alephnerd认为，MIPS转向RISC-V是一个有趣但互补的尝试，特别是在拥有芯片设计、制造和封装的端到端流水线方面，并且看到了RISC-V领域人才和资本的聚集。

Product News, Industry Insights, Announcements, and More
GlobalFoundries to Acquire MIPS to Accelerate AI and Compute Capabilities
July 8, 2025
Acquisition will expand GF portfolio with cutting-edge RISC-V processor IP and software tools for real-time computing in autonomous mobility, industrial automation, datacenter and intelligent edge applications
MALTA, N.Y., and San Jose, Calif., July 8, 2025
– GlobalFoundries (Nasdaq: GFS) (GF) today announced a definitive agreement to acquire MIPS, a leading supplier of AI and processor IP. This strategic acquisition will expand GF’s portfolio of customizable IP offerings, allowing it to further differentiate its process technologies with IP and software capabilities.
“MIPS brings a strong heritage of delivering efficient, scalable compute IP tailored for performance-critical applications, which strategically aligns with the evolving demands of AI platforms across diverse markets,” said Niels Anderskouv, president and chief operating officer at GlobalFoundries. “Through this acquisition, we will expand our capabilities to offer customers more flexible, RISC-V-based open platform solutions, paired with our differentiated process technologies and world-class manufacturing to help them build world-class products. This acquisition will be a powerful step forward to push the boundaries of efficiency and performance across a broad range of applications in automotive, industrial and datacenter infrastructure.”
MIPS recently expanded its processor IP offerings, based on open RISC-V specification, with the launch of its Atlas portfolio, a comprehensive suite of compute cores designed for real-time and application processing as well as specialized AI edge processing cores. Additionally, MIPS also introduced Atlas Explorer, a virtual platform that enables optimization of performance, power and area to shift-left in the design cycle.
“Becoming part of GlobalFoundries marks the start of a bold new chapter for MIPS,” said Sameer Wasson, CEO of MIPS. “GF’s proven track record in delivering differentiated technologies through a secure, global manufacturing footprint will enhance our ability to accelerate innovation and scale our solutions—unlocking new opportunities in the Physical AI space and driving even greater value for our customers.”
The acquisition of MIPS is subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions, including the receipt of required regulatory approvals, and is expected to be completed in the second half of 2025. Following the acquisition, MIPS will continue to operate as a standalone business within GF and serve its customers across a broad range of technologies.
About MIPS
MIPS is the leading provider of compute subsystems for autonomous platforms in automotive, industrial, and embedded markets. With a 40-year heritage in RISC computing innovation and safety capable processing, MIPS is uniquely positioned to simplify the adoption of Physical AI in industrial robotics and automotive applications. MIPS technology is based on the open specification RISC-V instruction set architecture, featuring MIPS pioneering, patented, multi-threaded capabilities to move beyond proprietary legacy architecture lock-ins. For more information, please visit MIPS.com.
About GF
GlobalFoundries (GF) is a leading manufacturer of essential semiconductors the world relies on to live, work and connect. We innovate and partner with customers to deliver more power-efficient, high-performance products for the automotive, smart mobile devices, internet of things, communications infrastructure and other high-growth markets. With our global manufacturing footprint spanning the U.S., Europe and Asia, GF is a trusted and reliable source for customers around the world. Every day, our talented and diverse team delivers results with an unyielding focus on security, longevity and sustainability. For more information, visit www.gf.com.

data.title: On The Meaning of Ritual
data.author: jger15
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：荀子思想中 ritual（礼仪/仪式）的现代意义及其应用

不同观点：
• buntsai 认为作者强调 ritual 的重要性是有道理的，但建议创造新 ritual 则是自大和天真的。他指出，中国在2500年前失去了支撑社会的 ritual 实践，并质疑是否应该简单地发明新的 ritual。他还通过提到阿道司·赫胥黎的《美德之后》（After Virtue）来警告创造新 ritual 的危险性，特别是与极权主义政权（如轴心国）的关联。
• polivier 分享了个人经历，强调 ritual 带来的安慰感，尤其是在面对生活中的重大事件（如出生、购房、退休、失去亲人等）时。他描述了如何通过特定的仪式行为（如喝特别的酒）来应对这些时刻，并从中获得平和感。
• eszed 认为评论中对 ritual 的讨论偏离了文章中的定义。文章中的 ritual 概念非常宽泛，涵盖了任何社会行为或社会假设，而不仅仅是传统意义上的仪式。他建议可能需要一个更贴切的术语来描述这个概念。
• alganet 对使用东方哲学文本持谨慎态度，尤其是当这些文本被用来操纵西方观众时。他质疑是否可以通过“西方视角”将所谓的“古老智慧”应用于现代生活，并特别提到文章中建议的21世纪统治意识形态的道德和有效性。
• marcus_holmes 反对文章中关于权威主义的核心假设，即人类天生会为了资源而争斗，因此需要国家权威来维持秩序。他认为，大多数人能够在没有外部强制的情况下合作，并建立和谐的社区。他承认暴力的存在可能需要权威的干预，但总体上质疑权威主义的必要性。
• indiebat 认为，关于古代仪式或神话的宏大宣称并不自动使其伟大。他建议，从西方经典（如莎士比亚、蒙田）中获取智慧更为实际，并质疑东方哲学是否真的比西方哲学更有深度。
• pessimizer 认为 ritual 是一种浪费资源的行为，但它通过展示承诺和牺牲来建立信任。他指出，昂贵的仪式可以 discourage 多重承诺，并通过 sunk cost fallacy（沉没成本谬误）来增强对某一团体或目标的忠诚度。尽管语气较为冷淡，他承认 ritual 在建立信任和承诺方面的实际效用。
• gerdesj 认为“ritual”一词在讨论中被过度使用，并质疑是否应该深入探讨圣经、托拉和古兰经等其他宗教经典。他认为这种讨论是无意义的“自慰”。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提到 ritual 的定义问题，特别是其在现代社会中的应用和意义。
• 关于是否应该创造新 ritual，以及古代 ritual 在现代社会中的价值，存在明显争议。
• 一些评论者质疑东方哲学在西方背景下的适用性，并建议从西方经典中获取智慧。
• 对 ritual 的功能和效用存在不同看法，有人认为它带来安慰和秩序，有人则认为它是浪费资源或与权威主义有关。

data.title: Particle Lenia Deluxe Edition
data.author: CraftingLinks
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了**Particle Lenia Deluxe Edition**，一个基于细胞自动机**Lenia**的项目，该项目通过GPU加速实现了3D粒子模拟，支持多物种粒子交互，并引入了多种更新核函数，带来了类似**Particle Life**的复杂行为模式。该项目受Alexander Mordvintsev等人的**Particle Lenia**研究启发，使用**Three.js**和**WebGPU**技术实现。文章简要说明了粒子在能量场中的运动规律，即粒子通过最小化排斥力和最大化生长力来移动，从而产生复杂的行为模式。文中还提供了源代码链接和模拟演示，鼓励读者自行探索。

44470447.article_content:
Particle Lenia Deluxe Edition.
Lenia
is a family of cellular automata that produces lifelike behaviors and patterns, first described in the seminal paper by Bert Wang-Chak Chan.
This project is heavily inspired by the original
Particle Lenia
research by Alexander Mordvintsev et al., which implemented a particle-based version of Lenia in Python and
JAX
.
Recognizing the importance of scale (number of particles) for simulation dynamics and iteration times for rapid pattern exploration,
I ported the simulation to the GPU and made it 3D. I also added several update kernels in addition to the original Gaussian one and programmed in
support for multi-species particle simulations which opens up a whole new breed of Mathematical Lifeforms, some that behave very reminiscent to critters found in
Particle Life
.
This port was achieved using compute shaders within
Three.js
and the (still unofficial)
Three.js Shading Language (TSL)
.
You can explore the Particle Lenia universe yourself at the bottom of this post
on the condition that your browser supports
WebGPU
and you have a graphics card with enough muscle to crunch the numbers.
The source code for the Particle Lenia implementation can be found
here
, go wild.
A too short intro to Energy Fields and Particles in Particle Lenia
The
energy field
is defined as
where
is the
repulsion field
and
the
growth field
(typically generated by two different convolution kernels). Particles follow the motion law
i.e.
they drift toward lower energy by simultaneously minimizing repulsion
and maximizing growth
. The rich behaviors you see are purely emergent from these local interactions and, to a lesser extent, the choice of kernels (the Mexican-Hat kernel is a personal favorite).
If you’re interested in the math, I encourage you to read the exposition in the original
Particle Lenia paper
.
It only requires that you understand what a ‘gradient’ is (ask an LLM) and how to apply the chain-rule for finding the differential equations.

data.title: A compact bitset implementation used in Ocarina of Time save files
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了用于《塞尔达传说：时之笛》存档文件中的16位位集（bitset）实现。该位集用于高效存储大量单比特标志，如"与NPC对话"或"打开宝箱"等状态。位集通过将标志存储在`uint16_t`数组中实现，每个16位字存储16个标志，最多支持4096个字（65536个标志）。其优点包括简单、无依赖、空间高效、快速、可扩展，并且标志ID直观易于调试。文章提供了C和Rust的示例代码及API参考，展示了如何设置、获取和清除位集中的标志。这种方法虽然在技术上不新颖，但因其简洁有效而具有实用价值。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OoT（Ocarina of Time）游戏中的16-bit坐标ID用于索引bitset的新颖性及其应用

不同观点：
• orlp：认为OoT中的bitset设计并不新颖，只是通过前4位指示位位置，其余位指示数组索引，属于标准的bitset实现。同时指出16-bit表示方式便于调试，但整体设计并没有特别的优势。
• Const-me：提到C++中的std::vector<bool>实现了类似的功能，但由于无法直接访问内部整数数组，导致序列化效率低。

OoT Bitset
The simple, no‑frills flag system used in
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
Implemented in C / C++,
and
Rust
Need to pack
hundreds (or thousands) of one‑bit flags
—“talked to an NPC”, “opened a chest”, etc.—into a save file without wasting bytes?
Ocarina of Time
solved this by storing flags in an array of
uint16_t
words.
oot_bitset
offers the same trick!
I learned about this technique from reading the
OoT decompilation project
source code.  See the
original code
that implements these flags for OoT's save file event information tables.
Why use it?
The bitset used in OoT is the simplest possible implementation of a bitset. It
is not new or novel. It is not fancy or full of features, but it has some nice
properties that is
good enough
for many use cases.
Simple, header‑only, zero deps
– drop a header (C) or add a tiny dependency (Rust). No heap, no
alloc
.
Space‑efficient
– 1 ×
u16
word = 16 flags. Scale from 1 to 4096 words (65 536 flags).
Fast
– branch‑free bit‑twiddling; compiles to a handful of instructions.
Scalable
– need 10 flags or 10 000? Just resize the array.
Intuitive IDs for debugging
– 0x12 maps to first word, second bit.
I wrapped this into a library because I haven't seen this pattern implemented
anywhere, and wanted to have a library I could use in my projects. I also
thought it was a neat bit of OoT lore for software engineer zelda enjoyers.
Why its cool
One clever aspect of how Ocarina of Time uses bitsets is that the first 4 bits
of a 16-bit flag ID directly indicate which bit is set. For example, the
ID 0xA5 means “set the 5th bit of the 10th 16-bit word” — the A (10 in decimal)
selects the 10th word, and the 5 selects the 5th bit within that word.
This works neatly because the word size is 16 bits: 4 bits are enough to index
any bit within a 16-bit word, and it also aligns nicely with a nibble for
debugging. If you switched to 32-bit words, you’d need 5 bits to index the bits
within the word, which no longer fits cleanly into a single nibble.
TL;DR: The flag ID encodes both the word and the bit — it’s the coordinate of the bit!
Bits
15…4
(12 bits)
3…0
(4 bits)
Use
word index
bit index
Max
0–4095 words
0–15 bits
These form a grid, and you can create UIs that visually map these coordinates
to a visual editor:
Hacker news folks say this is not that new or interesting, but I thought it
was! I hope some others find it interesting as well.

44467607.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了用于《塞尔达传说：时之笛》存档文件中的16位位集（bitset）实现。该位集用于高效存储大量单比特标志，如"与NPC对话"或"打开宝箱"等状态。位集通过将标志存储在`uint16_t`数组中实现，每个16位字存储16个标志，最多支持4096个字（65536个标志）。其优点包括简单、无依赖、空间高效、快速、可扩展，并且标志ID直观易于调试。文章提供了C和Rust的示例代码及API参考，展示了如何设置、获取和清除位集中的标志。这种方法虽然在技术上不新颖，但因其简洁有效而具有实用价值。

data.title: Bootstrapping a side project into a profitable seven-figure business
data.author: jonkuipers
data.article_summary: Kyle Nolan分享了他通过自力更生（bootstrapping）将副业ProjectionLab发展成一个年收入达100万美元的成功企业的历程。从2021年开始，Kyle受财务独立运动启发，因找不到合适的财务规划工具而自行开发ProjectionLab。经过四年的努力，从最初每月150美元的收入增长到2025年的83.3K美元。这一路充满了挑战和情绪波动，Kyle多次想要放弃，但最终通过坚持和组建团队取得了成功。他强调，创业过程如同乘坐过山车，而“不放弃”是成功的关键。Kyle还分享了找到合适的增长与营销伙伴Jon Kuipers，并逐渐建立团队，使企业持续增长的经验。最终，ProjectionLab不仅帮助了超过10万家庭规划财务未来，也实现了Kyle自己的财务独立目标。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：创业过程中的坚持与策略，市场验证，产品定价与功能，创业中的利润与收入问题，以及外部合作与机会

不同观点：
• **坚持与市场验证的重要性**：[bruce511] 认为在坚持与固执之间保持平衡很难，但市场验证（如早期使用量的增加）是必要的，有助于避免浪费时间。他强调了营销（如写博客、推广、运营Discord服务器等）对成功的重要性，并指出营销比单纯编码更有助于成功。
   
• **市场实际操作中的偏差**：[feizhuzhuzheng] 认为很多人讨论某些成功方法，但实际上只有极少数人真正做到了，暗示了理论与实践之间的差距。

• **地域差异与工具可用性**：[CalRobert] 提到在欧洲缺乏像美国那样好用的工具，但随后发现该工具在荷兰可用，表明地域差异对产品接受度的影响。

• **产品使用体验与未来期望**：[Crisco] 作为长期用户，赞赏产品的功能增加，并希望未来能看到更大的成功（如年收入达到1000万美元）。

• **个人使用与市场验证的关系**：[rorylaitila] 表示自己只能销售和构建自己经常使用的产品，以避免信号弱和倦怠，认为个人使用是市场验证的一种方式。

• **外部合作与机会主义**：[ilamont] 警告新创业者要小心那些试图在创业初期获取过多股权的“合作伙伴”，并分享了自己遇到的机会主义者的例子。

• **对增长与成就的祝贺**：[dvrp] 和 [nico] 对成就表示祝贺，并欣赏透明地分享起伏的细节。

• **产品定价争议**：[mNovak] 认为该领域仍然供不应求，但对基本计划的年费表示不满，认为一次性“基本”计划不合理。

• **利润与收入的平衡**：[mdorazio] 对未提及利润表示失望，强调创业者应关注实际可支配收入而不仅仅是收入增长，警告收入增长不等于利润。

• **产品功能建议**：[yesimahuman] 作为用户，建议增加实时证券价格功能，以避免手动复制粘贴数值。

• **股权分配猜测**：[vladmk] 猜测该帖子会带来更多收入增长，并猜测股权分配比例可能为60/40。

• **市场验证的定义与规模**：[ipaddr] 质疑从第一笔销售到每次峰值和下跌时的市场验证时机，并指出找到5个付费用户不代表能达到每月百万收入，质疑产品验证的具体含义。

补充讨论：
• 用户[montakaoh] 和 [pinkmuffinere] 对创业的成功表示祝贺，并分享了个人对创业过程中的起伏感受，强调 perseverance（坚持不懈）的重要性。

总体来看，讨论围绕创业中的策略、市场验证、产品定价与功能、利润与收入的平衡以及外部合作与机会主义展开，展示了创业过程中的多方面挑战与成功要素。

Jun 30, 2025
Bootstrapping a side project into a profitable seven-figure business in four years.
We really did it! We bootstrapped ProjectionLab to $1,000,000 in annual recurring revenue.
And I’m still processing that this is real. 🥹
Back in 2021, I was inspired by the financial independence movement and wanted a better way to plan my own life. I couldn’t find the right tool, so I started building.
I had no idea that side project would one day help over 100,000 households plan for their financial future too.
How we got here
If this is your first time hearing about ProjectionLab, here’s a quick recap:
Milestone
Date
What Was Happening

May 2021
First internet dollar! (from a
post to HN
)

blog post
$1K MRR

Shoutout from Mr Money Mustache

Whoah, public speaking?!
$8.3K MRR

Started to believe I could do this
$10K MRR
Jun 2023
The final boss of indie hacking
$16.6K MRR
Sep 2023
Dropped to part-time at my day job
$23.3K MRR
Nov 2023
Quit my day job and went all-in!
$41.6K MRR
Jul 2024
Started growing the team
$45.8K MRR
Aug 2024
Shared story on ChooseFI
$83.3k MRR
Jun 2025
👋 Here we are!
When you look beyond the recurring revenue chart, this journey had ups, downs, and moments I wanted to quit.
The emotions behind the numbers
Want to know what building in public from zero to a million dollars a year really felt like? NOT like serenely progressing up-and-to-the-right…
More like riding a dopamine rollercoaster while getting attacked by a bear.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
The flat months in the early years? The dips in earnings? The times I woke up to a dozen canceled subscriptions?
Each one had me questioning everything, wondering if I should just focus on the corporate ladder, or maybe try to get into big tech instead.
The financial independence movement is what set me on this path. So on top of worrying about normal business risks, I was primed to think in terms of my time and opportunity cost, and how failure would hurt my own timeline to FI.
But gradually, I learned that emotional peaks and valleys are always a part of entrepreneurship. And that “not giving up” is actually a superpower.
Not giving up
There are loads of people out there smarter than me.
But luckily, success indexes less on IQ and more on consistency. The willingness to doggedly show up every single day can take you to some really suprising and amazing places.
And you know what makes it easier and more rewarding to be that persistent?
Working alongside people you like.
From solo dev to real team
For the first two years, I burned the candle at both ends working solo. 4-6 hours every night after work, entire weekends, holidays, you name it.
404 Day Off Not Found.
That was the only way I could build something this complex in a crowded market as a risk-averse engineer with a day job. And I was fortunate enough to attempt this at a stage in life when I had lots of energy and few family responsibilities.
Plus my trusty sidekick, BB the bird:
But long-term, I knew there would be a choice to face:
Keep doing everything myself and watch growth plateau, or…
Find someone with a complementary skillset and start building a team.
I was just an ordinary engineer with zero marketing experience. So I figured I should try to team up with someone good at growth & marketing.
Finding a growth & marketing partner
During the first few years, I was approached by dozens of potential “partners.” Several wanted an outsize equity stake to essentially just make suggestions. Others had the wrong skillset or didn’t feel like a complete fit.
But
Jon Kuipers
jumped right into the trenches and worked to prove himself before asking for anything. He spent a year contributing real value, and when the time came to bring on a growth partner full-time, I didn’t look anywhere else.
Now I stay focused on building, while he handles growth, marketing, partnerships, and some ops stuff.
Building a team
We’ve also added a few contractors to the team.
And these guys are legends. 💪
They come straight from the ProjectionLab user community, and they are doing a great job fielding the arcane finance questions our customers love to ask. Plus hosting 1-on-1 sessions, creating
tutorial videos
, and more.
Could we have offshored customer success for pennies on the dollar instead? You bet. But having a happy and engaged user community of product evangelists means a lot to us, and I want them all to have the best experience possible.
For multiple years, I was up at all hours answering support questions myself. It interrupted my dev work (and my sleep) constantly. I love the PL community – it’s a big part of what motivated me to keep going back then.
And it blows my mind that the empty discord

• **个人使用与市场验证的关系**：[rorylaitila] 表示自己只能销售和构建自己经常使用的产品，以避免信号弱和倦怠，认为个人使用是市场验证的一种方式。

• **外部合作与机会主义**：[ilamont] 警告新创业者要小心那些试图在创业初期获取过多股权的“合作伙伴”，并分享了自己遇到的机会主义者的例子。

• **对增长与成就的祝贺**：[dvrp] 和 [nico] 对成就表示祝贺，并欣赏透明地分享起伏的细节。

• **产品定价争议**：[mNovak] 认为该领域仍然供不应求，但对基本计划的年费表示不满，认为一次性“基本”计划不合理。

• **利润与收入的平衡**：[mdorazio] 对未提及利润表示失望，强调创业者应关注实际可支配收入而不仅仅是收入增长，警告收入增长不等于利润。

• **股权分配猜测**：[vladmk] 猜测该帖子会带来更多收入增长，并猜测股权分配比例可能为60/40。

• **市场验证的定义与规模**：[ipaddr] 质疑从第一笔销售到每次峰值和下跌时的市场验证时机，并指出找到5个付费用户不代表能达到每月百万收入，质疑产品验证的具体含义。

补充讨论：
• 用户[montakaoh] 和 [pinkmuffinere] 对创业的成功表示祝贺，并分享了个人对创业过程中的起伏感受，强调 perseverance（坚持不懈）的重要性。

总体来看，讨论围绕创业中的策略、市场验证、产品定价与功能、利润与收入的平衡以及外部合作与机会主义展开，展示了创业过程中的多方面挑战与成功要素。

data.title: Plants monitor the integrity of their barrier by sensing gas diffusion
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: 文章主要探讨了植物如何通过气体扩散感知并修复其屏障组织——周皮的完整性。在拟南芥根部，当周皮受损时，乙烯和氧气通过伤口扩散，分别导致乙烯信号和缺氧信号的减弱，从而促进周皮再生。当修复完成后，这些信号水平恢复正常。这种机制帮助植物防止水分流失和病原体入侵，并在茎部受伤后也通过类似方式重建屏障。周皮的再生对植物生存至关重要，其机制研究具有重要生物学和经济价值。尽管周皮形成已研究多年，但其具体机制仍未完全理解。

Plants monitor the integrity of their barrier by sensing gas diffusion
Download PDF
Download PDF
Subjects
Cell fate
Plant hormones
Plant regeneration
Wounding
Abstract
Barrier tissues isolate organisms from their surrounding environment. Maintaining the integrity of the tissues is essential for this function. In many seed plants, periderm forms as the outer barrier during secondary growth to prevent water loss and pathogen infection
1
. The periderm is regenerated when its integrity is lost following injury; however, the underlying mechanism remains largely unknown, despite its importance for plant survival. Here we report that periderm integrity in
Arabidopsis
roots is sensed by diffusion of the gases ethylene and oxygen. Following injury of the periderm, ethylene leaks out through the wound and oxygen enters, resulting in attenuation of ethylene signalling and hypoxia signalling. This condition promotes periderm regeneration in the root. When regeneration is complete and barrier integrity is re-established, pre-injury levels of ethylene and hypoxia signalling are regained. Gas diffusion monitoring is also used to re-establish the barrier in inflorescence stems after the epidermis is injured. We thus propose that gas diffusion is used by plants as a general principle to monitor and re-establish barrier integrity.

Main
The periderm is a protective outer tissue established during secondary growth in many seed plants. It consists of several layers containing three different cell types: the phellem, phellogen and phelloderm
1
,
2
(Fig.
1a
). The outermost cell type, phellem (also known as cork), differentiates from the outer daughter cells of dividing phellogen cells. The differentiating phellem cells deposit lignin and suberin in their cell walls to form a physical barrier to protect secondary tissues from biotic and abiotic stresses
1
. As the periderm is the interface between the plant’s internal tissues and its environment, it is prone to injury. Periderm is re-established at wound sites in tree trunks, potato tubers and some fruits (such as apple)
3
,
4
,
5
. Periderm regeneration at wound sites is critical to prevent water loss and pathogen entry through wounds
4
. In addition to being essential for survival, the phellem of some tree species (such as cork oak) has been used by humans as manufacturing material for thousands of years. Understanding the mechanisms of periderm re-establishment would therefore have substantial biological and economic value. Even though the formation of periderm at wounds has been studied for more than a century, its underlying mechanism is still largely unknown.

data.title: Ceramic: A cross-platform and open-source 2D framework in Haxe
data.author: -yukari
data.article_summary: Ceramic利用Haxe编程语言的跨平台特性，实现了一次编写代码，即可将其转译为C++、JavaScript或C#。这使得应用能够原生导出到多个平台，包括Windows、Mac、Linux、iOS、Android、HTML5/WebGL，甚至集成到Unity项目中。Ceramic为开发者提供了高效的跨平台开发解决方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Haxe语言的优缺点及其应用场景

不同观点：
• gr4vityWall认为Haxe是一个有趣的语言，尤其赞赏其内置的imgui支持。他还指出，如果15年前Haxe专注于改善工具和人体工学以支持Web开发而非游戏开发，它有可能取代TypeScript的地位。
• themerone承认Haxe语言本身不错，但认为它未能兑现其承诺。特别指出其API在不同后端之间不够一致，导致难以在复杂应用中跨后端使用。
• mattigames提到Haxe缺乏移动输入的例子，而在当今游戏开发中，移动平台是主要的游戏平台，这可能是一个不足。

补充讨论：

data.title: Fast cryptographically safe GUID generator for Go
data.author: sdrapkin
data.article_summary: 该文介绍了一个名为 "guid" 的 Go 语言库，用于快速生成加密安全的全局唯一标识符（GUID）。该库提供了多种函数来生成和解析 GUID，包括 `guid.New()` 生成新 GUID，`guid.NewString()` 生成 Base64Url 格式的新 GUID 等。根据基准测试，`guid` 库的性能显著优于其他类似库，如 `github.com/google/uuid` 和 `nanoid`，在多 goroutine 环境下也能保持高效。该库还支持 JSON 序列化和反序列化，GUID 可以作为值或指针类型处理。安装可通过 `go get` 命令完成。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：UUID/GUID 生成器的安全性、实现细节及其使用场景

不同观点：
• saclark11 认为，将 UUID/GUID 生成器宣传为加密安全是一个错误。UUID 主要用于需要唯一标识但不依赖于不可猜测性的场景，V4 UUID 规范指出不应将其用作安全凭证。尽管 V4 UUID 可以生成具有一定安全性的标识符，但它仅有 122 位熵值，且不应被称为安全令牌。如果需要安全令牌，应使用如 Go 的 `crypto/rand` 这样的工具。

• deathanatos 指出，如果一个生成器不遵循 RFC 规范，就不应称之为 GUID，建议使用其他术语。同时指出有许多其他替代方案。

• amluto 对该实现的线程安全性提出质疑，并指出其底层使用了全局状态，这可能导致问题。此外，代码的缓冲处理类似于旧式 C 语言的处理方式，且缺乏最佳实践，比如回溯保护。如果程序分叉，可能会产生问题。建议使用高层次的工具如 vDSO getrandom()，而不是重新实现不正确的版本。

• imiric 提到速度与安全性之间的权衡，认为速度过快的 UUID 生成器可能更容易受到暴力攻击。imiric 使用 Cuid2 作为替代方案，因为它足够快且安全、防碰撞，满足 UUID 的大部分需求。

• sdrapkin 强调了该生成器速度上的优势，比标准 `github.com/google/uuid` 包快约 10 倍，并寻求社区反馈。

• CafeRacer 建议加入时间戳信息以使 UUID 可排序，类似于 uuid v7 的功能。

补充讨论：
• saclark11 还提到了 Go 团队在 `math/rand` 和 `math/rand/v2` 包中使用 CSPRNG 作为防御措施的例子，但仍建议在安全场景下使用 `crypto/rand`。

• sdrapkin 进一步指出 `guid.Read()` 是比 `crypto/rand` 更快的一种选择，并提供了链接供参考。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于 UUID 生成器是否应被视为加密安全，以及在何种情况下可以使用 UUID 作为安全令牌。
• 实现细节如线程安全性、全局状态的使用以及缓冲处理方式也引发了讨论。
• 速度与安全性之间的平衡也是一个讨论重点，部分用户认为速度快的生成器可能不够安全。
